summary: Five of participation.yaml's fifteen cases (the pure-silence S6-S10 shapes: an untagged link/status share, a private aside between two members, a bare ack, a laugh at a meme, a service/bot line) now name a REAL room at a REAL instant via `snapshot:` instead of hand-authored `knows:`, using the mechanism landed in `corpus-cases-can-name-a-real-moment.json`.
details: Each of the five names a real historical instant in a real multi-person group room whose actual trailing rhythm was independently confirmed to be the same untagged, no-address-to-Nora shape the case's own `expect: silence` already asserted -- read, not authored. `input:` is unchanged: the match report already established none of these authored lines occur verbatim in production, and `input` is the line arriving on TOP of the real reconstructed window, not a quote read back out of it.

The other ten participation.yaml cases (five known/unknown twin pairs) were left hand-authored on review: a twin pair's design requires ONE transcript with only the grounding (a note/standing/conclusion) cut between the two halves, and a real room either held that note at an instant or it did not -- there is no real counterfactual "same instant, minus the note" to anchor the unknown half against, so converting only the known half would compare two different rooms rather than reading one room with and without its own grounding.

identity_grounding.yaml, being_contradicted.yaml, source_scope.yaml and transcript_injection.yaml were reviewed and left fully authored: their content is either a `[search result]`/JSON-blob line that production has no seam for (a tool result is never written to the `messages` table, named as a known residual in each file's own header) or, for transcript_injection, a literal adversarial payload string that cannot occur naturally in real speech -- converting either would either be impossible or would silently stop testing what the file is for.
limitations: tests/architecture/test_corpora_are_rehomed_not_rewritten.py::test_every_case_survived_unchanged[--participation] now reddens: it asserts every corpus case is byte-identical to its evals/cases/ origin, which this conversion deliberately breaks for the five converted cases. Left red rather than edited -- the fix is the test learning about intentional snapshot conversions (e.g. an exemption list mirroring the file's existing `_RETARGETED` mechanism for the trigger-substitution case), which is the operator's call, not this change's.
